purpose: Thin separator line that visually splits content into groups. Renders as a full-width hairline (`horizontal`) or full-height hairline (`vertical`), and can carry centered content (an "Or"-style label) when the default slot or `label` prop is set. Unlike `ScrollArea` it adds no scrolling behaviour; it is a purely decorative-yet-semantic boundary exposing `role="separator"`.
useWhen: Separate groups of content inside a card, form, panel or menu.
An "Or" break between two alternative paths (social sign-in and email) with `label`.
A vertical rule between inline items in a toolbar or meta line.
avoidWhen: The break between two page sections → use `section-gap`.
A bounded region that scrolls → use `scroll-area`.
related: section-gap` — the frame that divides page sections, with its own rules and vertical air.
scroll-area` — scrolling container; Separator adds no scrolling.
bestPractices: Size a vertical divider through its wrapper (`flex h-4 items-center`); its own `h-full` beats a height class passed to it, and in an `items-center` row it collapses to zero height.
Keep `label` to a word or two; the default slot replaces it when you need inline markup.
Use it to separate groups, not to add spacing; it renders `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`.
